headline: Long-end rates still the dominant driver; crypto leverage is unwinding further (Hyperliquid OI z30 -2.1, Fear & Greed z30 -2.3) with ETH and SOL weakest
tldr: Measured against the app's own 30-day baselines, crypto is de-risking: Hyperliquid perp OI is about $11.9B (z30 -2.1), ETH OI z30 -2.3, SOL OI z30 -2.6, Fear & Greed fell to 59 from 64 (z30 -2.3) and BTC funding on HL is near zero (z30 -4.1). BTC $82.4K (-0.6% 24h), ETH $2,493 (-3.0%), SOL $110.4 (-4.2%). Macro and equities levels are carried from Oct 5-6 (no fresh close found): Fed funds 3.75-4.00%, 10Y ~5.3%, S&P 500 7,773.95. hl-cycles still reads strong risk-on for BTC (0 of 6 stress conditions) while its Macro lens is Restrictive (32). Watch: Sep CPI Oct 14, Oct 18 sanctions deadline, FOMC Oct 27-28. Not financial advice.

domains.summary: Policy is tightening: the FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 (first hike since 2023) and 16 of 18 participants projected at least one more hike this year. Long yields spiked on Oct 5 (10Y about 5.34%, 30Y about 5.70%, highest since 2002) and eased slightly on Oct 6 (10Y about 5.27%). We read the liquidity backdrop as tightening. No September CPI print or current oil/dollar levels could be verified this run. Update: a prediction-market snapshot from Oct 2 put the odds of an October hike near 26% while another source says roughly even, so we treat hike odds as unresolved; September CPI is scheduled for Oct 14 (August headline was 3.4% YoY). Brent was reported above $100 in early October and slipped below on Oct 6 (low-confidence, secondary sources). hl-cycles Macro lens is 32 (Restrictive), -21 points over 30 days.

US cash market status at write time unknown; levels are as of the Oct 5-6 sessions. Indexes are near record highs despite the rates spike, with AI-linked names accounting for the bulk of 2026 index gains per Jefferies. Volatility was subdued at the last verified reading (VIX 15.31 on Oct 2). No put/call or Oct 7 close found. No Oct 7-8 closes could be retrieved this run, so levels remain as of Oct 5.

Live Hyperliquid snapshot plus the app's rolling baselines. Perp OI totals about $11.9B across 234 listed markets (z30 -2.1 versus a 30-day mean of roughly $13B); ETH OI $2.75B (z30 -2.3), SOL OI $0.62B (z30 -2.6), HYPE OI $1.68B (z30 -1.5), BTC OI $3.28B (z30 -0.5). BTC hourly funding on HL has collapsed to ~0 (z30 -4.1) from the 0.00125%/h baseline, ETH funding is ~0.00013%/h. Marks: BTC $82,411 (-0.6% vs prior-day px), ETH $2,493 (-3.0%), SOL $110.42 (-4.2%), HYPE $85.50 (-2.2%). Fear & Greed 59 (from 64; z30 -2.3, unusual), DVOL 37.5 (z30 +0.8), total crypto mcap $2.77T (z30 -1.8), BTC dominance 59.1%, stablecoin cap $311B (z30 -1.1). We read this as leverage unwinding with majors holding up better than ETH/SOL; BTC dominance is steady. Low-confidence on causal links to rates.

Individual mega-cap quotes for Oct 6-7 could not be found this run, so dispersion is not assessed. Context: AI-linked stocks drove more than 80% of S&P 500 gains in 2026 per Jefferies, hyperscaler 2026 capex estimates run $520-725B depending on scope, and NVDA is about 22% of SMH, keeping semis breadth concentrated. Oct 2 coverage described semis as split.

The Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (signed Sep 18) requires implementation within 30 days (Oct 18), with authority for tariffs up to 100% on top importers of Russian energy, subject to waivers. Separately reported: US-Canada 50% tariffs after talks broke down (undated roundup), prospective new China overcapacity tariffs, new Iran-related Treasury sanctions, and an Iran-Oman Hormuz transit framework. Current Brent/WTI and OPEC+ news not found. Reporting this run adds that the US earlier threatened 50% tariffs on arms suppliers to Iran and that the Supreme Court struck down most reciprocal tariffs in February with the White House rebuilding via Section 301 (secondary sources; no fresh dated item for this week found).

thesis.observe: The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16; the 10Y was about 5.3% around Oct 5-6 and the S&P 500 closed at 7,773.95 on Oct 5 (later closes not found). On Hyperliquid, BTC is $82,411, ETH $2,493 (-3.0%), SOL $110.42 (-4.2%); perp OI is about $11.9B (z30 -2.1), ETH OI z30 -2.3, SOL OI z30 -2.6, BTC funding z30 -4.1. Fear & Greed is 59 (z30 -2.3). hl-cycles reads strong risk-on for BTC with 0 of 6 stress conditions active; its Compass headline is 48 (Neutral) and the Macro lens 32 (Restrictive). September CPI is due Oct 14; Russia/Iran sanctions deadline is Oct 18.
thesis.infer: Crypto positioning is thinning faster than price: OI and funding are several standard deviations below their 30-day norms while BTC holds above its short-term holder cost basis ($73.9K per hl-cycles). We read that as a leverage flush rather than a trend break, but with the 10Y near 5.3% and the Macro lens Restrictive the backdrop is not supportive. Consensus is pricing an uncertain October FOMC; we read September CPI as the swing input. Low-confidence.
thesis.forecast: Base case (we lean here, low-confidence): range-bound crypto with subdued leverage while long yields stay elevated. Tail case (low-confidence): a hot CPI or further long-end spike forces a repricing, and risk skews toward a sharper leg down in high-beta alts; hl-cycles would flag a daily close below $81.6K (ETF cost basis) as invalidating its risk-on read. Second tail case (low-confidence): the Oct 18 sanctions deadline broadens into a trade shock. Consensus is pricing a split October decision; we read the risk as hinging on September CPI.
thesis.disclaimer: Not financial advice. Market intelligence only — a reasoned read of public data, not a recommendation to buy or sell anything.

risks: Hot September CPI (Oct 14) or a further long-end yield spike (30Y above 5.7%)
Daily BTC close below ~$81.6K (ETF cost basis, per hl-cycles) would invalidate its strong risk-on read
Tariff/sanctions escalation around the Oct 18 deadline
Data-quality risk: equity, oil and mega-cap levels are from Oct 5-6 or earlier; Elfa/FRED series not available from the app this run
